content: {"rule": "K-G4", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text decides whether witnesses on the defender's 'cited in' line for C3 count as unanswered, which is the exact question K-G4 governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the \"witness left unanswered\" ground fails", "rule_words": "A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count.", "room": "'pressed against' the link: the judge could read the challenger's own later rounds as the pressing rounds, or require a quoted pressing sentence from an earlier defender-side round. I weighed both; the rule's wording ('the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it') points to a quoted pressing sentence, and the text supplies none.", "why": "The judge removes the unanswered-witness ground for C3 by pointing to the challenger's later rounds that quote the verses, without quoting any earlier round's sentence that pressed those verses against C3 and naming that round, and the audit itself records that no such PRESSED line exists."}
